read me first · ≈ 8 minutes

Before we bake

теория по-русски

Коротко о том, что мы учим в этом уроке, когда это ставить и как это звучит. Прочитай один раз до заданий и возвращайся сюда, если что-то забудешь. Все новые слова урока с переводом собраны внизу, в Glossary.

1. Исчисляемые и неисчисляемые

В английском каждое существительное либо можно посчитать штуками, либо нельзя. От этого зависит всё: a/an, -s, much или many.

Countable · считаемa cookie → two cookies
an egg → three eggs
В единственном числе обязательно a / an / the / my: I want cookie → I want a cookie.
Uncountable · не считаемmilk, sugar, bread, cinnamon, coffee, rice, money, time, advice, news, information, furniture, work, weather
Без a/an и без -s: some bread, a bread, breads.

Глагол после неисчисляемого — в единственном числе

  • The news is good!Новости хорошие! (news — одно целое, не «новости» во множественном)
  • This advice was really useful.Этот совет оказался очень полезным.

Ловушка для русскоговорящих

По-русски «совет», «новость», «мебель», «хлеб», «работу» можно посчитать. По-английски advice, news, furniture, bread, work — нельзя. Нужен «счётчик»: a piece of advice, a loaf of bread, a job вместо a work.

2. Как посчитать неисчисляемое

Ставим «упаковку» или «порцию»: a … of. Считаем уже её: two slices of pie.

a slice ofpie, bread, cakeкусок (ломтик)
a piece ofcake, advice, newsкусок, штука
a loaf ofbread → two loavesбуханка
a pinch ofcinnamon, saltщепотка
a cup oftea, coffeeчашка
a carton ofmilk, juiceпакет
a bar ofchocolateплитка
a jar ofhoney, jamбанка

Одно слово — два смысла

Многие слова бывают и такими, и такими. Смысл меняется:

coffeeкофе вообще: I love coffee.
a coffeeчашка кофе в кафе: Two coffees, please!
cakeпирог как еда: Have some cake.
a cakeцелый торт: She baked a cake.
hairволосы: She has long hair.
a hairодин волос: There's a hair in my soup!
timeвремя: I don't have time.
a timeраз, случай: We had a great time.
experienceопыт: She has a lot of experience.
an experienceслучай, впечатление: a strange experience
roomместо: Is there room for me?
paper / a paperбумага / газета
3. Сколько? much, many, a lot, a few…
с неисчисляемыми
(milk, time)		с исчисляемыми во мн. ч.
(eggs, people)
многоmuch, a lot of, plenty ofmany, a lot of, plenty of
немного, хватаетa littlea few
мало, почти нетlittlefew

much и many — в вопросах и отрицаниях

  • Is there much sugar in it?Там много сахара?
  • We didn't have much time.У нас было мало времени.
  • She drinks a lot of tea.В утвердительном — a lot of, а не much tea. Но too much / so much можно: You put too much sugar in!

plenty of = больше, чем нужно

  • Don't hurry, we've got plenty of time.Не спеши, времени полно.

a little / little, a few / few — сравни

  • She has a few friends here.У неё тут есть несколько друзей (и это хорошо).
  • She has few friends here.У неё тут почти нет друзей (грустно).
  • Add a little cinnamon.Добавь немного корицы.

Только only a few и only a little: We only have a little time, а не only little time.

of почти не слышно

  • a cup of tea/ə ˈkʌp əv ˈtiː/ — в речи «э ка́пэ ти», отсюда разговорное a cuppa
  • a lot of people/ə ˈlɒt əv ˈpiːpl/ — «э ло́тэв пи́пл»

Ударение меняет часть речи

  • fresh produce/ˈprɒdjuːs/ сущ. «продукты с фермы» — ударение на ПЕРВЫЙ слог
  • to produce/prəˈdjuːs/ глагол «производить» — ударение на ВТОРОЙ

Слова урока, где легко ошибиться

Типичные ошибки

  • an advice → some advice / a piece of advice
  • informations, furnitures → information, furniture
  • The news are… → The news is…
  • much people → many people / a lot of people
  • He travels much. → He travels a lot.
5. Рецепты: until, once, when

В рецепте Мии есть ещё одна грамматика. Это юнит 25 из Grammar in Use.

После when, once, as soon as, until — настоящее время

Даже если речь о будущем, will после этих слов не ставим:

  • Stir the milk until it thickens.Помешивай, пока не загустеет. (не will thicken)
  • Once the milk is hot, add the pumpkin.Как только молоко нагреется, добавь тыкву.
  • I'll call you when I get home.Позвоню, когда приду домой. (не when I will get)

Действие уже закончилось — present perfect

  • When you have filled the mugs, add the cream.Когда нальёшь (уже налила), добавь сливки.
  • Don't open the oven until the cake has risen.Не открывай духовку, пока пирог не поднимется.

Как пишут рецепты

Глагол в начале, без you: Pour the milk… Stir in the vanilla… Отрицание — Don't: Don't let it boil!

once/wʌns/ как только (и «однажды»)
until/ənˈtɪl/ пока не, до тех пор пока
as soon as/əz ˈsuːn əz/ как только, сразу как

≈ 12 minutes

Reading

Mia, 23, left her office job and opened a tiny café in York. She keeps a notebook behind the counter. Guess the highlighted phrases from context first — then tap to check.

Notes from The Little Acorn

a notebook kept behind the counter · by Mia

Monday, 7 October

I opened the café at seven, and by ten past seven the whole street knew about it. It's the smell: the of fresh coffee out of the door, mixed with cinnamon and something sweeter. A man in a grey coat came in “just for a ” and stayed for a slice of pumpkin pie and two coffees. I didn't have much time to chat — there were people in the queue — but before he left, he gave me : “Never put too much nutmeg in anything.”

Wednesday, 9 October

Lesson learnt: bake a few extra loaves on Wednesdays. We ran out of bread before lunch, because students from the college arrive . They don't want , they want . So I've started a little : soup, home-made bread and , all — students have very little money. Everything is made from from the market: no , no . My granny would be proud.

Friday, 11 October

Disaster before breakfast. A carton of milk had overnight, and the cream . and a broken fridge are not friends. I threw everything away (the last thing I need is to give somebody ) and made the lattes with oat milk instead. Nobody complained. In fact, a few people asked for it again.

Sunday, 13 October

The pumpkin spice latte is a strange drink. Some customers order it every day; others say it's far too sweet and it . For me, black coffee was : I hated it at fifteen. Now I've it, but I still love the of my own pumpkin latte. The secret? Real pumpkin, cinnamon, a little nutmeg — and not too much sugar.

Tonight the whole café still smells of cinnamon. I'm sitting with a cup of tea and a biscuit, tired but happy. I've had very little sleep this month, but I've had a lot of new experiences, and I've learnt more than in a whole year of work at the office.

True or false?
Mia opens the café in the evening.
The man in the grey coat had pie and two coffees.
The set menu is expensive.
Nobody liked the lattes with oat milk.
Show answers
  1. Mia opens the café in the evening. — False (at seven in the morning)
  2. The man in the grey coat had pie and two coffees. — True
  3. The set menu is expensive. — False (it is reasonably priced)
  4. Nobody liked the lattes with oat milk. — False (nobody complained, and a few people asked for them again)
Answer, then check
1. Why did the man in the grey coat come in?
Show answer
He smelt the coffee and cinnamon from the street — he came in “just for a whiff”.
2. Why did Mia start a set menu?
Show answer
Students arrive dying of hunger, they want a decent meal, and they have very little money.
3. What went wrong on Friday?
Show answer
The milk had gone sour and the cream smelt off, because the fridge was broken.
4. What is the secret of Mia's pumpkin latte?
Show answer
Real pumpkin, a pinch of cinnamon, a little nutmeg and not too much sugar.

≈ 15 minutes

Grammar

countable & uncountable · much, many, a few, a little. Mia uses them in every note. Work them out yourself first, then open the rule.

from Mia's notebook
  1. He stayed for a slice of pumpkin pie and two coffees.
  2. We ran out of bread. Bake a few extra loaves!
  3. He gave me a piece of advice.
  4. Students have very little money.
  5. A few people asked for it again.
Coffee is uncountable. So why two coffees?
Check
In a café, a coffee = a cup of coffee. Two coffees = two cups.
Why a few loaves, and not a few breads?
Check
Bread is uncountable. We count it with a loaf / a slice / a piece of bread.
Can you say an advice or advices?
Check
No. Advice is uncountable: some advice, a piece of advice.
little money but few people: which word goes with which kind of noun?
Check
little / much + uncountable (money, time, sugar); few / many + plural (people, eggs).
Which is positive: a few people asked or few people asked?
Check
A few = some, enough to notice (good news). Few = almost nobody (bad news).
Show the rule
RuleExample
Countable: a/an, plural -s, numbers
Grammar in Use, unit 69		a cookie, two cookies, an egg
Uncountable: no a/an, no -s, verb in singular
unit 69		some bread, The news is good.
a … of to count uncountable things
unit 69B		a slice of pie, a loaf of bread, a piece of advice
two meanings: coffee / a coffee, hair / a hair, time / a time
unit 70		Two coffees, please. There's a hair in my soup!
much / little + uncountable
many / few + plural
unit 87		not much time, many eggs, very little money, few friends
a lot of, plenty of + both
unit 87A		a lot of tea, plenty of people
a little / a few = some (positive)
little / few = not enough
unit 87C–E		a few friends ≠ few friends
an advice → some advice
The news are good → The news is good
She drinks much tea → She drinks a lot of tea
only little time → only a little time

≈ 5 minutes

Words in the tin

Mia is tidying her kitchen. Can you count it or not? One egg, two eggs — but one honey, two honeys? Sort the pictures.

What goes in the tin?

Tap a picture, then tap the top or the bottom of the tin — it goes in. Tap it in the tin to take it out again.

you can count an egg, two eggs
you can't count some honey
Show answers
  1. you can count: egg, cookie, apple, pumpkin, acorn, leaf — an egg, two apples, a few acorns, autumn leaves
  2. you can't count: honey, flour, milk, cinnamon, butter, sugar — some honey, a little milk, a pinch of cinnamon, a bar of butter

Count the pot, not the honey: a jar of honey, a carton of milk, a bag of flour. Coffee, cake and chicken can be both — that's why they're not in the tin.

≈ 12 minutes

Mia's recipe

Mia finally wrote down her famous pumpkin latte. Read the recipe, put the steps in order, then learn the verbs every recipe uses.

you will need

Mia's Pumpkin Spice Latte

for 2 mugs · 10 minutes

  • 2 cups of milk (or oat milk)
  • half a can of pumpkin purée
  • 2 shots of strong coffee
  • 1 tablespoon of sugar, or a little honey
  • a pinch of cinnamon — and a little more for the top
  • a pinch of nutmeg
  • a few drops of vanilla
  • some whipped cream

method

Oh no — Mia spilt coffee on the page and the steps got mixed up. Tap them back into order. One step is not from this recipe!

Put the mugs in the freezer for an hour.Take the pan off the heat and stir in the vanilla.Once the milk is hot, whisk in the pumpkin, sugar and spices.Pour the milk into a small pan and heat it gently.When you have filled the mugs, top them with cream and sprinkle with cinnamon.Let it simmer until it thickens a little — don't let it boil!Pour the coffee into two mugs and add the pumpkin milk.
Show answers
  1. Pour the milk into a small pan and heat it gently.
  2. Once the milk is hot, whisk in the pumpkin, sugar and spices.
  3. Let it simmer until it thickens a little — don't let it boil!
  4. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the vanilla.
  5. Pour the coffee into two mugs and add the pumpkin milk.
  6. When you have filled the mugs, top them with cream and sprinkle with cinnamon.

The extra step: Put the mugs in the freezer for an hour. Brrr.

A. Cooking verbs

Tap a meaning from the box — it goes opposite the highlighted verb.

let a liquid flow outcook just below boilingmake warm or hotmake solid things liquidcut into small piecesmix slowly with a spoondrop a little on topmix fast
Show answers
  1. whisk — mix fast
  2. stir — mix slowly with a spoon
  3. simmer — cook just below boiling
  4. pour — let a liquid flow out
  5. sprinkle — drop a little on top
  6. melt — make solid things liquid
  7. chop — cut into small pieces
  8. heat — make warm or hot
B. until, once, when Grammar in Use 25

После when, once, as soon as, until — настоящее время, даже если речь о будущем. Если важно, что действие уже закончилось, — present perfect.

1. Stir the milk until it .
2. Once the milk hot, add the pumpkin.
3. When you the mugs, add the cream.
4. Don't open the oven until the cake .
5. As soon as the latte ready, sprinkle it with cinnamon.
6. I'll make you a latte when you home.
Show answers
  1. thickens
  2. is
  3. have filled
  4. has risen
  5. is
  6. get

No will after when / once / until: the future is already clear from the main part — add, sprinkle, I'll make.

In this picture I can see plenty of small orange pumpkins — there must be at least forty of them. There isn't much room between them: they are piled on top of each other. A few of them still have their stems. It reminds me of a market in October — the smell of wet leaves and a whiff of cinnamon from a café nearby. I'd use a few of them for soup and one for a pie.
